summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Ryuken Sato was an emeritus professor at Taisho University and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute, both attested in 2014.
Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at To-ji as 東寺総学 and also taught at Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Lausanne by 2003, studying under Tom Tillemans.
Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a professorship at Shuchiin University, attested in 2014 and 2026.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, Ryushin Saito was a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and a faculty member at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Ryushin Sudo studied at Taisho University circa 1949–1953, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He later served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryushin Uryuzu studied at Ryukoku University (circa 1951–1955). He held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (circa 1972–2003).

Ryusho Hikata studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and received a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor and dean at Kyushu University, president of Fukuoka Women's University, and a Japan Academy member.

Ryuta Kikutani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. His career includes posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015), Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020), and Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 2026).

Ryutaro Tsuchida studied at the University of Tokyo and Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1979–1983) and held a professorship at the University of Tokyo from 1983, becoming emeritus professor (1995–2012).

Ryutoku Kimura studied at Komazawa University (~1966–1970). He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1980), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and chief priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).
Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryuyu Saito studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.

Ryōmin Akizuki studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1948). A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Makio Takemura, he held a post at Saitama Medical University from around 1972 to 1991.
Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, Rüdiger Schmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1962–1965). He served at Saarland University from circa 1968 to 2004.
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indology scholar who held positions at the Institut de France (attested 1994) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2004–2005 and 2024).

An Indology scholar, S. Bhaskaran Nair served at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, where he held positions as general editor (attested 1944 and 1992) and deputy director (attested 1974–1977 and 1986).
An Indology and linguistics scholar, S. D. Laddu was attested at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1968 and served as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 2003.

S. G. Dani studied at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research under M. S. Raghunathan (~1969–1975). In Indology and history/archaeology, he worked in Mumbai (~1969–2012) and was a professor at IIT Bombay (~2013–2017).
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology, serving as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, both attested in 1982.
